name: Pierre Auger Observatory
summary: A large Argentine cosmic-ray observatory also performs dedicated ultra-high-energy neutrino searches using inclined air showers and Earth-skimming tau signatures.
detection_principle: Water-Cherenkov surface stations measure shower timing and particle content. Neutrinos can generate unusually young, electromagnetic-rich inclined showers, unlike ordinary cosmic-ray showers that have traversed much more atmosphere.
technologies: Water-Cherenkov surface stations for neutrino air-shower searches

status.label: Operating / data taking
status.evidence: An operating multipurpose observatory with a documented dedicated neutrino-search programme; cosmic-ray detections are not classified as neutrino discoveries.

timeline.event: Surface-detector exposure used in the principal neutrino analyses began.
Diffuse and directional neutrino searches using data through August 2018 published.

collaboration.name: Pierre Auger Observatory Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Additional instrumentation
key_parameters.value: Fluorescence telescopes and AugerPrime upgrades support the wider cosmic-ray programme

results.summary: No neutrino candidates were found in the approximately 14.7-year exposure. Diffuse and source-specific upper limits constrain ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray production scenarios.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
